title: Build an AI Research Agent: Apoorva Joshi
talk_summary: A beginner workshop introducing AI agent concepts (planning, memory, tools) and then building a LangChain research agent with arXiv tools, MongoDB vector store, and short-term chat memory. It is mostly conceptual and framework-specific, with little measured evidence or production insight.

takeaways.technique: ReAct thought/action/observation loop with explicit stop condition
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt the LLM to emit a thought, an action with arguments, then an observation from the tool result, looping until a stop sequence signals the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: after each action we ask the LM to make an observation based on information or feedback obtained from the previous action and plan what action to take next

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a generate-then-critique loop several times before finalizing, optionally using a separate LLM or agent as the critic.
When a conversation grows too long, either keep only the most recent messages or summarize the history, accepting some information loss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: some solutions to do that are things like retrieving the end most recent messages or summarizing the conversation at the cost of some information loss

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap the agent runnable in a message-history wrapper that persists chat history to a database keyed by session ID.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by default it organizes the chat history using a session ID that you pass in uh along with your input query or prompt

takeaways.technique: Descriptive tool schemas for function calling
takeaways.what_they_do: Define tools as functions with descriptive names, detailed descriptions, and typed arguments so the LLM picks the right one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you typically use a descriptive tool name uh specify which function to call Provide a pretty detailed description of what exactly the function does
